label: es-e6d1
change: The bundled lib.dll becomes a value of the game's rules: OriginalGameRules.library: OriginalLibData? (new engine/Sources/NTSDCore/OriginalLibData.swift; stored in the immutable Roles, compared in ==; nil in LF2 2.0a's OriginalGameRules.lf2 default; NTSDProfile and the synthetic pack set it). The application's sessions are modelled only with the library: OriginalApplicationBootstrap.start (the single start: HostSession, ObservedStartup, WindowStartup, the Runtime), OriginalApplicationMatchLaunchSession.init and OriginalApplicationGameplaySession.init throw the typed OriginalLibData.Required before any change when it is absent; OriginalApplicationInputSession sets the library's commands only with it (else the word-1 path). The passes keep choosing their paths from their own arguments.
publicSurface: OriginalGameRules.init(..., library:) and OriginalGameRules.lf2(..., library:) (new parameter, default nil)

tests.engine: SyntheticLibraryTests (3): the LF2 default and engineTests have no library, the synthetic pack has it; rules differing only in the library are unequal; the recovered startup on the pack's inputs with library-less rules throws Required before staging an attempt (prepare and failedAttempt never called) and commits no startup, session or batch; 164 engine tests in debug
tests.native: NTSDProfileLF2Tests: NTSD carries the library and with(...) copies keep it unless they replace it; the family test compares library; NTSDProfileTestRules.with gains library: (outer nil keeps, .some(nil) clears)

required.finding: OriginalLibData's doc claimed the passes take their pristine paths without the value; no pass reads rules.library
required.done: reworded: the sessions read it at their entries; the passes choose from their own arguments

verified: NTSD neutrality: every place that builds rules is covered (NTSDProfile and its identity set the library; native tests use NTSDProfile.rules or with copies; engineTests is pass-level only; syntheticPack sets it)
guards before any state change; Required public, Equatable, Sendable; Bootstrap.start is the single production start
InputSession: without libraryCommands only PostDrawCommands reads it and keeps the word-1 spawn
== includes library; with(library:) double-optional semantics right
guards read only lets: no runtime exclusivity checks added
optionalAdopted: the startup test asserts the guard runs before any attempt is staged
the LF2 family test compares library
optionalRecorded: no direct test of the match-launch and gameplay guards or the input session's branch: production cannot reach them without the library because Bootstrap and the catalog take their rules from the same identity
unguarded entries reached only after a guarded Bootstrap.start: OriginalApplicationMenuSession.init(state:loop:) (public, no rules), the catalog session (guarded in E6d-2) and the loaded menu session
the full init's library defaults to nil: a game building its own rules loses it silently but fails loudly at Bootstrap start (the ntsd-2.8.3.3 branch starts with nil)
